title: Indefinite Integrals
text:
4.2 The Computation of Indefinite Integrals

Theorem 4.1 If \(F\) and \(G\) are antiderivatives of \(f\) and \(g\) on an interval \(I\), then \(\lambda F + \mu G\) is an antiderivative of \(\lambda f + \mu g\) on \(I\). Consequently, \[
\int \bigl(\lambda f(x) + \mu g(x)\bigr)\, dx
= \lambda \int f(x)\, dx
+ \mu \int g(x)\, dx.
\]


Theorem 4.2 If \(F\) and \(G\) are antiderivatives of \(f\) and \(g\), respectively, then \[
\int f(G(x))\, g(x)\, dx
= F(G(x)) + C.
\]


Theorem 4.3 If \(F\) and \(G\) are antiderivatives of \(f\) and \(g\) on an interval \(I\), then \[
\int F(x)\, g(x)\, dx
= F(x) G(x) - \int G(x)\, f(x)\, dx.
\]

Examples

Compute \[
\int \frac{x}{1+x^{2}}\, dx.
\]
Let \[
y = 1 + x^{2}, \qquad dy = 2x\, dx.
\]
Then \[
\int \frac{x}{1+x^{2}}\, dx
= \frac{1}{2} \int \frac{1}{1+x^{2}}\, d(1+x^{2})
= \frac{1}{2} \int \frac{1}{y}\, dy.
\]
Thus \[
\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{y}\, dy
= \frac{1}{2}\ln|y| + C
= \frac{1}{2}\ln(1+x^{2}) + C.
\]
Compute \[
\int \frac{1}{\cos^{2m} x}\, dx.
\]

Let \[
t = \tan x, \qquad dt = \sec^{2}x\, dx = \frac{1}{\cos^{2}x}\, dx.
\]
Then \[
\int \frac{1}{\cos^{2m} x}\, dx
= \int \frac{1}{\cos^{2m-2} x}\, d(\tan x)
= \int (1+t^{2})^{\,m-1}\, dt.
\]
Thus the integral can be reduced to a polynomial-type integral in \(t\): \[
\int \frac{1}{\cos^{2m} x}\, dx
= \int (1+t^{2})^{\,m-1}\, dt,
\qquad t=\tan x.
\]

Compute \[
\int f(\cos^{2} x)\, dx.
\]

We first rewrite the integrand: \[
\int f(\cos^{2} x)\, dx
= \int \frac{f(\cos^{2} x)\,\cos^{2}x}{\cos^{2}x}\, dx.
\]
Let \[
t = \tan x, \qquad dt = \frac{1}{\cos^{2}x}\, dx, \qquad
\cos^{2}x = \frac{1}{1+t^{2}}.
\]
Then \[
\int f(\cos^{2} x)\, dx
= \int \frac{1}{1+t^{2}}\, f\!\left(\frac{1}{1+t^{2}}\right)\, dt.
\]
Thus the integral of \(f(\cos^{2}x)\) is transformed into an integral in \(t\): \[
\int f(\cos^{2} x)\, dx
= \int \frac{1}{1+t^{2}}\, f\!\left(\frac{1}{1+t^{2}}\right)\, dt,
\qquad t=\tan x.
\]

Compute \[
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{x^{2}+a^{2}}}\, dx
\]
Let \[
\theta = \arctan\!\left(\frac{x}{a}\right)
\]
Then \[
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{x^{2}+a^{2}}}\, dx
= \int \frac{1}{\sqrt{a^{2}\tan^{2}\theta + a^{2}}}\, d(a\tan\theta)
\]
Since \[
\sqrt{a^{2}\tan^{2}\theta + a^{2}}
= a\sqrt{1+\tan^{2}\theta}
= \frac{a}{\cos\theta},
\]
we have \[
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{x^{2}+a^{2}}}\, dx
= \int \frac{1}{\cos\theta}\, d\theta
\]
Let \[
t = \sin\theta,
\qquad dt = \cos\theta\, d\theta .
\]
Then \[
\int \frac{1}{\cos\theta}\, d\theta
= \frac{1}{2}\int \left(\frac{1}{1-t} + \frac{1}{1+t}\right) dt
= \frac{1}{2}\ln\frac{1+t}{1-t} + C
\]
Thus \[
\frac{1}{2}\ln\frac{1+\sin\theta}{1-\sin\theta} + C
\]
Since \[
\sin\theta = \frac{x}{\sqrt{a^{2}+x^{2}}},
\]
we get \[
\frac{1}{2}\ln
\left(
\frac{1+\frac{x}{\sqrt{a^{2}+x^{2}}}}
      {1-\frac{x}{\sqrt{a^{2}+x^{2}}}}
\right)
= \ln\left(x+\sqrt{a^{2}+x^{2}}\right) + C_1.
\]
Therefore \[
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{x^{2}+a^{2}}}\, dx
= \ln\left(x+\sqrt{a^{2}+x^{2}}\right) + C .
\]
Let \[
I_n = \int e^{x}\sin^{n}x\, dx .
\]
Then \[
I_n = \int e^{x}\sin^{n}x\, dx
= \int \sin^{n}x\, d(e^{x})
= e^{x}\sin^{n}x - \int e^{x} d(\sin^{n}x).
\]
Compute the differential: \[
d(\sin^{n}x)
= n\sin^{\,n-1}x \cos x\, dx.
\]
Hence \[
I_n
= e^{x}\sin^{n}x - n\int \sin^{\,n-1}x \cos x\, e^{x}\, dx.
\]
Rewrite the integral: \[
I_n
= e^{x}\sin^{n}x - n e^{x}\sin^{\,n-1}x\cos x
+ n\int e^{x} d(\sin^{\,n-1}x\cos x).
\]
Thus \[
I_n
= e^{x}\bigl(\sin^{n}x - n\sin^{\,n-1}x\cos x\bigr)
+ n(n-1)(I_{n-2} - I_n) - n I_n .
\]
Solve for \(I_n\): \[
I_n
= \frac{
e^{x}\sin^{\,n-1}x\bigl(\sin x - n\cos x\bigr)
+ n(n-1)I_{n-2}
}{n^{2}+1}.
\]
Special case: \[
I_1 = \frac{e^{x}(\sin x - \cos x)}{2}.
\]
A rational function is a quotient of two polynomials:
\[
R(x)=\frac{P(x)}{Q(x)}, \qquad P, Q \in \mathbb{R}[x], \quad Q(x)\neq 0.
\]
To integrate \(R(x)\), follow these steps.
Polynomial Long Division
If \[
\deg P \ge \deg Q,
\] divide \(P\) by \(Q\): \[
\frac{P(x)}{Q(x)} = S(x) + \frac{A(x)}{Q(x)},
\qquad \deg A < \deg Q.
\] Thus, \[
\int R(x)\,dx = \int S(x)\,dx + \int \frac{A(x)}{Q(x)}\, dx.
\]
Factor the Denominator
Factor \(Q(x)\) into irreducible real factors:

\[
Q(x)=
\prod (x-a_i)^{k_i}
\prod (x^2 + b_j x + c_j)^{m_j},
\]
where each quadratic satisfies \[
b_j^2 - 4c_j < 0.
\]
Partial Fraction Decomposition \[
\frac{A_1}{x-a} + \frac{A_2}{(x-a)^2} + \cdots + \frac{A_k}{(x-a)^k}
\]
\[
\frac{A_1x+B_1}{x^2+bx+c}
+ \frac{A_2x+B_2}{(x^2+bx+c)^2}
+ \cdots +
\frac{A_mx+B_m}{(x^2+bx+c)^m}.
\]
Integrate Each Term \[
\int \frac{1}{x-a}\, dx = \ln |x-a| + C.
\]
\[
\int \frac{1}{(x-a)^k}\, dx
= \frac{-(x-a)^{-k+1}}{k-1} + C \qquad (k\ge 2).
\]
\[
x^2+bx+c = \left(x+\frac{b}{2}\right)^2 + d, \quad d = c-\frac{b^2}{4}.
\]
\[
\int \frac{1}{(x+\frac{b}{2})^2+d}\, dx
= \frac{1}{\sqrt{d}} \arctan\!\left(\frac{x+\frac{b}{2}}{\sqrt{d}}\right) + C.
\]
\[
\int \frac{x+\frac{b}{2}}{(x+\frac{b}{2})^2+d}\, dx
= \frac{1}{2}\ln\left((x+\frac{b}{2})^2+d\right) + C.
\]

\[
  I_n = \int \frac{1}{(1+x^2)^n}\,dx
  \qquad (n\ge 2).
  \]
Write
\[
  I_n = \int \frac{1}{(1+x^2)^n}\,dx
  = \int \frac{(1+x^2)-x^2}{(1+x^2)^n}\,dx
  = I_{n - 1}
       - \int \frac{x^2}{(1+x^2)^n}\,dx.
  \]
\[
  \begin{aligned}
  &\int \frac{x^2}{(1+x^2)^n}\,dx
  = \frac{1}{2}\int \frac{x}{(1+x^2)^{n}} \,d(1 + x^2)
  = \frac{1}{2 (1 - n)}\int x \,d\left((1 + x^2) ^ {1 - n}\right) \\
  &= \frac{1}{2 (1 - n)} \left( \frac{x}{(1+x^2)^{n-1}} - \int \frac{1}{(1 + x^2)^{n - 1}} \, dx\right).
  \end{aligned}
  \]
Therefore
\[
  I_n
  = \left(1 - \frac{1}{2(n-1)}\right) I_{n-1}
    + \frac{1}{2(n-1)}\frac{x}{(1+x^2)^{n-1}}.
  \]
Thus the reduction formula is \[
  I_n
  = \frac{x}{2(n-1)(1+x^2)^{n-1}}
  + \frac{2n-3}{2(n-1)}\, I_{n-1},
  \qquad n\ge 2.
  \]
Together with
\[
  I_1 = \int \frac{dx}{1+x^2} = \arctan x + C,
  \]
\[
  \int R(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)\, d\theta
  =
  \int
  R\!\left(
  \frac{1 - t^{2}}{1 + t^{2}},\;
  \frac{2t}{1 + t^{2}}
  \right)
  \frac{2}{1+t^{2}}\, dt.
  \]

\[
\int R(x,\sqrt{x^{2}-1})\, dx
=
\int
R\!\left(
\frac{1+t^{2}}{1-t^{2}},\;
\frac{2t}{\,1-t^{2}\,}
\right)
\, d\!\left(\frac{1+t^{2}}{1-t^{2}}\right).
\]
